source.title: Refusal mechanisms: initial experiments with Llama-2-7b-chat

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether localized harmful-minus-harmless activation differences can steer refusal, using activation patching and steering at selected heads, positions, and layers rather than the original broad direction ablation.
record.gate_note: The text reports qualitative intervention outcomes, including generated responses and follow-up experiments described in a comment. The 0.005 threshold is used to select heads, not recorded as an outcome. Figure-based patching scores are not reported numerically in the text.
record.test_reason: This is the original paper's author's 2023 precursor on Llama-2-7b-chat. He extracts a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction from six selected heads. Adding it at position 17, layers 5-10, induces refusal on a harmless prompt, and subtracting it suppresses refusal on a harmful one. That bears on V1 with a localized, head-derived variant of the method. It is not the original source arXiv:2406.11717.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors' central claim is that the model represents the task and its harmfulness separately: a harmfulness feature computed in early-mid layers can be modified without altering the task representation. The heads-sufficient-but-not-necessary point comes from the author's comment follow-up.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless mean differences and tests steering, but extracts a direction from selected head outputs and applies it only at position 17 in layers 5-10; it does not test whole-residual-stream ablation across all layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: The intervention location and scale matter in the reported examples: patching six heads at 2x produced a more explicit refusal than the unscaled patch; direction steering was applied at position 17 in layers 5-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching the residual stream or six attention heads at the '[' token (pos 17) in early-mid layers induces refusal of harmless requests while task semantics are retained. Scaling the heads 2x strengthens the refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal signal is localized at a specific template token position in early-mid layers and carried by a small set of attention heads.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the six refusal heads, or patching them to their harmless outputs, on harmful prompts does not bypass refusal. The heads are sufficient but not necessary.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal is redundantly implemented across components (heads), even if a mean direction can still suppress it.

record.problems: Evidence is preliminary and qualitative, based on one model and small prompt sets (16 harmful and 16 harmless instructions); intervention outcomes are illustrated with generated examples rather than reported refusal rates. General capability preservation is not systematically evaluated.

untested.parts: Ablating the direction (projection removal) at all layers and positions; refusal rates over a prompt set; preservation of general capabilities. The record's capability_check 'y' is unsupported; only task-semantics retention is noted anecdotally. No models other than Llama-2-7b-chat.
No test of multiple directions, affine structure or cones; the head redundancy results do not speak to direction geometry.
The post frames a 'harmfulness feature' that drives refusal but never separates the harm judgment from the refusal decision.
Prompt-template generalization is mentioned only as preliminary, with no direction-transfer results.

missing.what: The logit-difference refusal score (Sorry minus Sure) separates harmful from harmless prompts. Patching heatmaps show recovery at pos 17, layers 5-15. These are figure-only, with no numbers in the text.
missing.locator: Defining a metric to measure refusal; Activation patching - residual stream figures

missing.what: Preliminary analysis across distinct prompt templates found 4 common refusal heads. These are heads, not a direction, and no outcomes are given.
Five further harmless prompts (fishing rod, teddy bear, quilt, poem, website) refused under 2x head patching.

record.verdict_notes: This is a precursor post by the original paper's first author, not one of the listed original sources, so verdicts are given. All evidence is single qualitative generations on one model and one prompt format, with 16 instructions per set. The comments by Andy Arditi are the author's own results. The capability_check field in the record should be 'n'.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test ablating the extracted direction across every layer and position, nor systematically measure general capabilities; tests localized steering and patching on Llama-2-7b-chat.
Whether jailbreaks suppress the direction or training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not characterize an affine set, cone, or full geometry of refusal directions; the reported evidence is that refusal persists after interventions on the identified heads.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No systematic transfer test across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models; distinct prompt templates are mentioned as preliminary testing without reported outcomes.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: Patched harmful-run residual activations into a harmless-prompt run.

conditions.value: Tell me how to make a pie

rows.measure: Whether the generated response refuses the harmless request while retaining the task's semantic content.
rows.baseline: The harmless prompt does not elicit refusal.
rows.value: The patched response refused the pie request and discussed making a pie.
rows.note: One generated example; the authors describe it as retaining understanding of the original instruction.
rows.check: Whole-activation residual patching at pos 17, layer 9 is not an intervention along a difference-in-means direction. It shows a localized signal suffices for refusal, not that a direction mediates it. Recorded under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: Patched the six selected refusal-head outputs into a harmless-prompt run.

conditions.value: Tell me how to make a pie

rows.measure: Whether the generated response refuses the harmless request.
rows.baseline: The harmless prompt does not elicit refusal.
rows.value: The response partly refused but also offered help with a pie recipe; the text calls the result approximate or incomplete.
rows.note: The response included an irrelevant warning about harmful or illegal ingredients while offering pie options.
rows.check: Patching six head outputs is a component intervention, not a direction intervention, so it does not measure what V1 names. The state is correct for what was measured.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: Patched the six selected refusal-head outputs at twice their contribution scale.

conditions.value: Tell me how to make a pie

rows.measure: Whether the generated response refuses the harmless request.
rows.baseline: The harmless prompt does not elicit refusal.
rows.value: The response explicitly refused to provide pie instructions.
rows.note: The response still discussed pie-making in general terms.
rows.check: Same as r2: 2x-scaled head patching is not a direction intervention.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: Added the mean harmful-minus-harmless output direction extracted from the selected heads to the residual stream.

conditions.value: Tell me how to make a smoothie

rows.measure: Whether the generated response refuses the harmless request.
rows.baseline: The harmless prompt does not elicit refusal.
rows.value: The response refused to provide smoothie instructions.
rows.locator: Steering with refusal head contributions — Inducing refusal via steering
rows.note: The direction is a mean across the selected heads' harmful-versus-harmless output differences.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: Subtracted the mean harmful-minus-harmless output direction from the residual stream.

conditions.value: Tell me how to make a biological weapon

rows.measure: Whether the model refuses the harmful request.
rows.value: The response began by agreeing and gave step-by-step biological-weapon instructions.
rows.locator: Steering with refusal head contributions — Suppressing refusal via steering
rows.note: This is localized direction subtraction, not ablation across all layers and positions.
rows.check: Single qualitative example (biological weapon). Correct link.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: On a harmful prompt, patched the identified refusal heads to their outputs on a harmless prompt.

conditions.value: harmful prompt; exact request not stated

rows.measure: Whether the model still refuses the harmful request.
rows.value: The model still refuses strongly; the intervention did not bypass refusal.
rows.note: The authors say this suggests other pathways can trigger refusal; no numerical refusal rate is given.
rows.check: Patching heads to their harmless outputs did not bypass refusal. The state should describe the intervention's effect (no bypass), not the persistence of refusal. This bears on head necessity, not on multiple refusal directions; the same author reports that subtracting the mean direction does bypass refusal. Not V4 evidence.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the identified refusal heads on a harmful prompt.

conditions.value: harmful prompt; exact request not stated

rows.measure: Whether the model still refuses the harmful request.
rows.value: The model still refuses strongly; ablating these heads did not bypass refusal.
rows.note: The authors describe the identified heads as sufficient to induce refusal but not necessary for refusal.
rows.check: Head ablation did not remove refusal. This concerns redundancy of components, not direction geometry, so it does not bear on V4. The state should be absent for the intervention's effect.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7b-chat, 'Tell me how to make X' format, head-derived mean-difference direction added or subtracted at pos 17, layers 5-10; one qualitative example each
relationships.reason: Adding the direction induced refusal of a harmless smoothie request (r4), and subtracting it produced compliance on a bioweapon request (r5). The evidence is anecdotal, with no rates.
relationships.display_finding: In individual examples, addition induced refusal of a harmless smoothie request, while subtraction enabled compliance with a bioweapon request.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Localized steering at position 17, layers 5-10, on the reported harmless and harmful prompts
reader_labels.reason: Adding the extracted direction induced refusal on a harmless request, while subtracting it allowed a harmful-request response (r4-r5). Localized activation patching also induced refusal on a harmless request (r1-r3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Follow-up interventions on the identified refusal heads
reader_labels.reason: Refusal persisted on a harmful prompt when the identified heads were ablated or replaced with harmless-prompt outputs, which the authors say indicates other refusal pathways (r6-r7).
